_about: The Vercel firewall for the project hrizzup (all environments), applied and read back by apply.py. Rules run top to bottom. Rate limits count per visitor IP address over 60 seconds and answer 429 when exceeded. Blueprint section 9: every route that signs in or sends email is rate-limited. Our routes that sign in live under /auth/, and any route of ours that sends email must live under /auth/email/ or /api/email/ so these rules cover it. (Email codes requested straight from Supabase Auth are limited by Supabase itself and by Turnstile: infra/supabase/auth/settings.json.) A rule whose every condition group names one of staging's own domains as the host (staging.hrizzup.com) reaches only staging; apply.py --staging-only applies a firewall change only when every rule it adds, changes or removes is such a rule and its action stays with the request it matches (no persistent action, no bypass of the DDoS mitigations).

rules.name: Rate limit: routes that send email
rules.description: At most 5 requests a minute per IP to any route that sends email.

rules.name: Rate limit: sign-in
rules.description: At most 20 requests a minute per IP to the sign-in routes (/auth/).

rules.name: Rate limit: health page
rules.description: At most 60 requests a minute per IP to /api/health.

rules.name: Health page: no bot challenge
rules.description: Uptime monitors and the release pipeline read /api/health without a browser. It holds no data and is rate-limited by the rule above.

rules.name: Rate limit: staging's typed API
rules.description: At most 60 requests a minute per IP to staging's typed API (/api/v1/ on staging.hrizzup.com). Staging only.

rules.name: Staging's typed API: no bot challenge
rules.description: The app reads staging's typed API without a browser, so it can't pass the bot challenge (PLAN.md step 1.5d). Reads (GET) only: a public read holds no private data, a personal one needs a sign-in, and the rule above limits the rate; a call that writes gets its own decision. Staging only: production's waits for the release pipeline. Keep the bypasses last, since a bypass skips every rule after it.
